correctness.rationale: The verifier constructs the explicit eleven-vertex, eighteen-edge bipartite graph, tests three-connectivity after every deletion of at most two vertices, and verifies a rotation-system sphere embedding with nine quadrilateral faces; odd order rules out Hamiltonicity and the classical uniqueness statement identifies the Herschel graph. It enumerates exactly 751 nonempty matchings with face vector (18,111,280,270,72), checks every signed boundary squared is zero, produces 367 valid face-coface pairs, and topologically sorts the complete 2502-arc reversed-matching Hasse graph to certify acyclicity. Exact integer cancellation yields a Morse CW complex with one vertex, two 2-cells and fourteen 3-cells, no 1-cells or higher critical cells, and a 2-by-2 unimodular minor in the 3-boundary, explicitly the identity columns. Since the 2-skeleton is a wedge of two 2-spheres and its pi2 is Z squared, two 3-cells cancel those generators and the twelve remaining ones attach to a contractible subcomplex, proving a wedge of twelve 3-spheres. Independent direct mod-two boundary ranks (17,94,186,72) and Euler characteristic -11 corroborate the calculation; they are not substituted for the integral or homotopy proof.

originality.rationale: The 2024 outerplanar matching-complex theorem cannot apply to the three-vertex-connected nonouterplanar Herschel graph; its discussion supplies no exact Herschel value. The 2004 bounded-matching graph complex is a different construction. The 2005 claw-free-independence result gives connectivity bounds, not an exact Herschel line-graph homotopy type. Published-index comparisons were made against both Herschel independence-complex results and Goldner-Harary/Franklin matching-complex results, none of which implies the present claim. Targeted terminology, line-graph aliases, exact Betti multiplicity, and own accessible scientific claims produced no equivalent statement. This is a best-knowledge originality conclusion, not proof of universal nonpublication.
residual_risks: No web or bibliographic search can exclude unindexed equivalent results or unpublished tables.
Wachs (2003), a relevant general matching-complex survey, was noted in a bibliography but its full text was not examined; no asserted noncoverage relies on it.
The 2004 and 2005 older papers were available in this comparison only through dated abstracts; they were not treated as whole-document noncoverage certificates.

value.rationale: The Herschel graph is the unique sparsest eleven-vertex non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graph, an intrinsically motivated canonical test object for matching-complex topology beyond the outerplanar regime. The calculation determines its complete integral homotopy type (not just face counts), distinguishes it from the mixed-dimensional Goldner–Harary matching-complex example at the same extremal vertex number, and provides a concrete positive wedge example among three-connected nonouterplanar graphs. Neither the twelve-sphere multiplicity nor the attaching-map trivialization follows from the general connectivity bounds or outerplanar homotopy theorem. This exact natural invariant has reusable comparative value without claiming a general planar classification.
